about: Havenbrooke's arcs for the director (dungeon/director.py), from dungeon/world/packages/havenbrooke/beats.json and hidden-truths.json, set in sophomore year. Each stage has its tier, what is true (truth), a seed the narrator may plant, and how it reaches a character who is not there (word). Drafts for Vanta to keep, change or cut.

arcs.name: Institutions that claim
arcs.seen: Every family, court and office with a claim on the third floor is starting to collect.

antagonist.name: the claimants
antagonist.agenda: to bring each of the six back under the family, court or office that thinks it owns them

stages.truth: A sylph diplomat is coming to see Rina unannounced, Genevieve Corwin has booked a layover in Syracuse, and the Crane gala list has two Nexus names on it.
stages.seed: A cream envelope on the common-room table, addressed in fountain pen to someone who does not live here.
stages.word: Someone on the third floor of Nexus is having a visit from family, and it is not going well.

stages.truth: The Eastern Seelie court sends an auditor with an envelope, a DED review board asks for files, and a cold case in Boston reopens.
stages.seed: A woman in a gray coat in the Grove at closing, asking the night staff about signatures.
stages.word: A fae auditor is asking questions in Haven, and the Fae Heritage Association has stopped returning calls.

stages.truth: The claims go to hearings: the court, the Federal Esoteric Court and the Council of Bloodlines all sit on matters with Nexus names in them.
stages.seed: A summons served in the Morrowe dining hall, in front of everyone.
stages.word: Three hearings in one spring, and the Oracle has the docket numbers.

arcs.name: The stolen sealskin
arcs.seen: A selkie senior's skin is gone from its warded chest, and campus security is calling it a dorm theft.

antagonist.name: Evander Crane
antagonist.agenda: to keep what he took, and keep the family from finding out he took it

stages.truth: Evander Crane stole Mairead's sealskin, and the Crane steward has been buying selkie-kin binding texts at Drothe's for months.
stages.seed: A selkie senior in the library with her hair gone brittle, rereading the same page.
stages.word: A selkie on campus has lost her skin, and nobody is saying it out loud.

stages.truth: There is an older sealskin in the Crane collection, and a selkie family in Maine has been looking for it since 1931.
stages.seed: A receipt from Drothe's in a coat pocket: three books on binding, paid in cash.
stages.word: Drothe will not sell certain books to certain buyers this month, and will not say why.

stages.truth: Sealskin theft is sentenced like aggravated assault, and the federal case would reach the Council of Bloodlines.
stages.seed: A DED field agent at Midnight Gas asking the cook about the Crane cars.
stages.word: The DED is asking about the Cranes, and the Cranes are asking who called.

arcs.name: Exposure fatigue
arcs.seen: Mundane students keep dropping out with "depression", and Evermere keeps the numbers to itself.

antagonist.name: the university
antagonist.agenda: to keep the numbers out of the papers and the scholarships funded

stages.truth: Since 2005 mundane students have been pulled from classes with what was undiagnosed exposure fatigue, and the files are in the Evermere intake records.
stages.seed: A human sophomore asleep in the library at noon, with the Evermere protocol pamphlet under his hand.
stages.word: Another mundane student went home mid-term, and the Oracle wants to know why.

stages.truth: The Oracle has a source and a set of files, and one of them is a scholarship student's from the third floor of Nexus.
stages.seed: An unsigned email with a spreadsheet attached and the subject line "you should see this".
stages.word: The Oracle is sitting on a story about the scholarship kids.

stages.truth: The story runs, the DED opens a review, and the university has to choose between its numbers and its students.
stages.seed: A front page on every table in Morrowe, and a Dean who cancels all her meetings.
stages.word: The exposure-fatigue story is out, and the DED has called the president.
